metadata.title: The Risk Register
metadata.creator: Sanjana Rao
metadata.note: ai-explainer CONCEPT explainer (AI + risk management) for @HumanitariansAI, first-person Sanjana Rao (af_bella). Framework = SCORE / OWN / WATCH: AI scores the known risks, you own the project-specific risk it can't see, you watch each with a trigger+owner.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- ClaudeComposerAsk, ask answered; first-person Sanjana
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sanjana, a project manager at Humanitarians AI. Here's a feature that sounds like magic: the AI in your project tools will now build your whole risk register for you. One prompt, and out comes a tidy list of risks, each scored by probability and impact. It feels like you've covered everything. But a risk register has one job -- to name the thing that actually sinks the project. So the real question is: can the AI see that one?

props.command: The AI in my project tools can auto-build and score a whole risk register. Can I trust it to catch the risks that actually matter?
output: AI scores the KNOWN risks fast -- probability x impact
but it only sees risks that fit a template
the one that sinks you is usually project-specific

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW -- hesitant-writer BLUF; corrects the reel's real misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea in one breath. It's tempting to treat the AI's risk register as your risk register. It isn't. It's a strong draft of the risks that fit a pattern -- and the risk that actually gets you is usually the one specific to your project, which no template has. The AI scores. You own what it can't see.

beats.role_note: SHOW-DON'T-TELL: AI fills the matrix with template risks; the real threat is off it
beats.narration_text: So here's what the AI gives you. Ask it for your risks, and it returns the usual suspects -- scope creep, a dependency slips, someone leaves -- each dropped onto a probability-by-impact grid. And honestly, it's good at this. These are real risks, scored consistently, in seconds. But look at where they come from: a template of what goes wrong on projects in general. The risk that actually sinks yours -- the one database expert who's out in March, the vendor only your lead knows is shaky -- isn't on the grid, because it was never in the template.

shot.visual_intent: A probability x impact grid (low/med/high each axis). AI drops template risk dots onto it (scope creep, dependency slip, attrition) -- tidy, mostly low/medium. Then a terracotta 'blind spot' dot appears OUTSIDE/off the grid labeled 'your project-specific risk' in the high-impact zone -- the one the template never had. Reframe: good at the known, blind to the specific.

beats.role_note: framework-first (PROOF): SCORE / OWN / WATCH, shown BEFORE any example
beats.narration_text: So before you trust any AI-built register, run three steps. One: score. Let the AI draft and rate the common risks -- it's fast and consistent on the known ones. Two: own. Add the risks only you can see -- the ones tied to your team, your vendor, your timeline -- because those never came from a template. Three: watch. Give every real risk a trigger and an owner -- the signal that says it's happening, and the person who acts. A register nobody watches is just a list. Score, own, watch.

shot.visual_intent: Three steps stacked: 1 SCORE (AI rates the known risks -- fast, consistent) 2 OWN (you add the project-specific risk AI can't see) 3 WATCH (each risk gets a trigger + an owner). Each with a short what-it-means line. Footer: a register nobody watches is just a list. Terracotta on the footer + on step 2 (the human-only step).

beats.role_note: ASK->RESULT LAW -- composer ask that generates the T05 register
beats.narration_text: Let's build a real one. Here's a software project near a deadline. Watch me ask the AI to draft and score the register -- but only the risks it can actually justify from what I give it, and to flag what it can't assess without me.

props.command: Draft and score a risk register for this project: probability and impact for each risk, pulled only from the plan I gave you. Don't invent risks to fill the page, and list separately anything you can't assess without project context I haven't provided.

beats.role_note: worked example walked through the framework -- score, then the human owns + watches
beats.narration_text: And there's the register -- six risks, each on the grid. Score? Solid: the common risks are rated sensibly, and I can see the reasoning. Now I own what it couldn't. The AI has no idea my one database expert is on leave the week we migrate -- high probability, high impact. I add it, top-right. Then watch: each serious risk gets a trigger -- 'migration date locked without a backup owner' -- and a name next to it. Now it's not a list. It's a plan.

shot.visual_intent: Left: an AI register table (6 rows) on a P x I mini-grid, all known risks. Apply SCORE check (green). Then the HUMAN adds a terracotta row -- 'DB expert on leave during migration' -- plotting top-right (high/high) with an OWN check. Then a WATCH column lights: trigger + owner tags appear on the serious rows -> a green 'ACTIVE PLAN' verdict. Terracotta on the added risk.

beats.role_note: falsifiability -- a calm all-green AI register that misses the one high-impact risk
beats.narration_text: Now the trap -- because a calm register is the most dangerous kind. Same tool, different project. The AI returns a beautiful grid: everything low-probability, low-impact, a wall of green. Looks like a safe project. But watch what's missing. The entire thing depends on a single vendor API with no contract and no backup -- a true high-impact risk. It's not scored low. It's just not there, because nothing in the template knew to ask. A green grid doesn't mean low risk. It can just mean the real one is off the page.

shot.visual_intent: A P x I grid full of green low/low dots -- looks safe. Then a red 'MISSING' marker lands in the empty high/high corner: 'single-vendor API, no backup' -- a high-impact risk that was never added. Verdict: a red 'LOOKS SAFE - ISN'T' / the real risk is off the grid. Terracotta/red on the missing-risk corner.

beats.role_note: reusable rubric restated -- AI SCORES the known; you OWN the unknown + WATCH
beats.narration_text: So here's the rule you can carry to any project. Let the AI score -- it rates the known risks faster and more consistently than you will. But you own the one it can't see, and you put a trigger and a name on every risk that matters. The AI fills the grid. You find the risk that isn't on it.

shot.visual_intent: A clean router: LEFT 'AI SCORES -- the known risks, fast'. A center gate = SCORE / OWN / WATCH. RIGHT 'YOU FIND -- the risk off the grid'. High negative space, terracotta accent on the gate.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW -- ClaudeComposerAsk 'Your turn.'; prompt read aloud + discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Next time a tool offers to build your risk register, don't just accept the grid. Run this prompt: have the AI score the risks it can justify, and -- separately -- list every assumption it had to make and everything it could not assess without knowing your team, your vendors, and your timeline. Read that second list closely. That's your map of blind spots, handed to you. A good answer tells you plainly what it couldn't see. A bad one hands you a wall of green and calls it safe -- and now you know to go find the risk that isn't on the page.

props.segment: Run it on your own project
props.command:
Build me a risk register for the project below.
[PASTE YOUR PLAN]

1. SCORE only the risks you can justify from the plan (probability x impact).
2. SEPARATELY list every assumption you made + everything you canNOT assess
   without my team, vendors, and timeline.
3. Do NOT invent risks to fill the page.
Give me (a) the scored register and (b) the 'blind spots' list.
